== Immune to Balefire?  Vulnerable to the True Power?  I don't think so. ==

I absolutely do not recall it being either mentioned or demonstrated ''anywhere'' in the books that cuendillar is somehow unaffected by Balefire.  Seeing as how Balefire actually burns away the ''Threads of the Pattern itself'' (essentially unraveling the very fabric of reality that corresponds to the object) rather than affecting the matter directly, it wouldn't even matter what kind of specific material was being affected, since the Pattern itself is dissolving around it.  Balefire is so destructive it dissolves the fabric of reality; no form of matter, regardless of how tough it is, could endure the destruction of the ''fabric of reality that it occupies.''

Neither did I see any indication in the books that the True Power was able to affect cuendillar while the One Power wasn't.  The Seals on The Dark Ones prison weren't crumbling because they were being affected by the True Power, they were breaking down from the ''direct touch of The Dark One.''  The Dark One is the embodiment of entropy and destruction, the antithesis of The Creator (so, uncreation); his (its?) presence causes matter to break down at the atomic (or probably even subatomic) level, and even causes The Pattern itself to start to unravel, again making it meaningless regarding what specific material is actually being affected.  Even if objects of cuendillar were someone single macroscopic atoms, The Dark One's touch would still cause them to come apart.
